notes.decision: Translated 'the Great One' (or 'the Greatness'). The form parallels ⲧϩⲛⲁⲟ (line 3) where the same root appears with feminine article. Best analyzed as ⲡⲉ-/ⲧ- + ϩⲛⲁⲟ where ϩⲛⲁⲟ is a Lycopolitan substantival form of ⲛⲁϭ 'great' (compare ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'greatness'). The epenthetic ϩ also appears in ⲛⲉϩⲁⲓⲱⲛ 'the aeons' (line 2), supporting a dialect feature. Functions here as a divine title.

Translated 'again, in turn' throughout. Per glossary, Lycopolitan ⲍⲱⲱϩ = Sahidic ϩⲱⲱϥ (intensive/reflexive). Here the structural function is enumerative ('the X also/in turn') rather than truly reflexive, marking parallel cosmic registers.
Translated 'runs' rather than 'flees.' The Spirit's downward motion through all the aeons reads as cosmological circulation/diffusion, not flight from danger.
ⲧⲁⲍⲙ = Sahidic ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'call, summon, invite.' ⲧⲁⲍⲙⲟⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ = 'they were summoned forth out from him' — emanative-vocative semantics: the divine call brings them out from the Father.

Translated 'the cosmos.' Recurs four times on this page (lines 15, 16, 18, 19) as the spatial domain at the second register, paired structurally with 'the elements' (third register) and 'the Church' (fourth). 'Cosmos' captures the technical Manichaean sense of the manifest world-system.
'The Mind of the Father.' ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ rendered 'mind' per mandatory terminology, here functioning as a cosmological hypostasis (the Father's noetic faculty), not the first of the five faculties.
Restored as 'the Virgin of Light' (παρθένος). Standard Manichaean cosmological figure. The fragmentary ending ⲡⲧⲁⲣ at line 18 + [ⲫⲉⲛ]ⲟⲥ at line 19 confirms the reading.
Lycopolitan ⲓⲱⲁⲙⲧ = ϣⲟⲙⲛⲧ 'three.' Feminine 'the third (one),' implicit referent ⲧⲉⲩⲁⲁⲓⲙⲟⲛⲓⲁ = 'the third Eudaimonia' in the enumerative scheme.
Translated 'Might' per glossary. The triad here is Eudaimonia / Sophia / Might (where Might = ⲧⲟⲁⲙ/ⲛⲟⲁⲙ, the third member). Capitalized as cosmic principle.
Tentatively 'those who exist/dwell.' The form is unclear — could be from ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'dwell' or possibly ⲟⲩⲱϣⲙ. Context (the Five Sons of First Man bearing up the All) suggests inhabiting/sustaining sense.
ⲧⲛⲁⲟ = 'the great' (feminine). Restoration ⲛⲉⲩⲁⲁⲓⲙⲟⲛⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟ ⲛⲉⲁⲩ follows the page's repeated formula 'their great Eudaimonia which is glory' applied to each register.

ⲛⲥⲁⲍ = 'the teachers' (Sah. ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ). ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲁⲍⲉ = 'those who teach' (Lycopolitan ⲙⲁⲍⲉ = ⲙⲁⲑⲉ from same root). The formula 'leaders and teachers who teach' is standard for the apostolic-ecclesiastical succession; matches ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ paradigm.
